summary: This week's Gulf technology and financial landscape is defined by accelerated enterprise AI deployment, major sovereign debt issuance, and deepening cross-border cybersecurity cooperation. Saudi Arabia anchored regional digital momentum through the LEAP 2026 conference, hosting significant AI infrastructure commitments including the upcoming NTT DATA AI Factory Lab in Riyadh and cloud integration MoUs from organizations like the Saudi Red Crescent and King Salman Park Foundation. Simultaneously, commercial AI adoption accelerated across the wider GCC, underscored by Dubai Chambers launching Agentic AI training for over 14,000 member companies and e& unveiling an offline-capable AI laptop in the UAE. In the financial sector, Saudi Arabia successfully priced a $3.25 billion dual-tranche USD sukuk, demonstrating sustained international liquidity demand. For C-suite and board executives in banking and government-technology organisations, these developments signal a structural shift from experimental AI pilots to industrial-scale execution, requiring immediate alignment on sovereign cloud architectures, workforce upskilling, and robust cross-border security frameworks.

stories.t: NTT DATA AI Factory Lab to Launch in Riyadh
stories.b: NTT DATA announced the establishment of an AI Factory Lab in Riyadh aimed at accelerating enterprise artificial intelligence adoption across the Middle East and Africa. The facility will serve as a regional hub for scaling industrial AI applications and technical capabilities.
stories.w: This initiative provides Gulf enterprises and government entities with localized, high-performance infrastructure to transition advanced AI models from development to production.

stories.t: Saudi Arabia Prices $3.25bln Dual-Tranche USD Sukuk
stories.b: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia successfully priced a $3.25 billion dual-tranche US dollar-denominated sukuk, drawing strong international investor demand following initial price thoughts set at tighter spreads.
stories.w: The successful sovereign issuance establishes a robust benchmark for regional financial institutions and large-scale digital infrastructure funding costs.

stories.t: Dubai Chambers Launches Agentic AI Training
stories.b: Dubai Chambers has rolled out a comprehensive Agentic AI training programme targeted at equipping more than 14,000 member companies with advanced autonomous AI capabilities.
stories.w: The programme addresses the region's skills gap by fast-tracking practical workforce readiness in autonomous workflows for thousands of local commercial entities.

stories.t: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan Sign Cybersecurity MoU
stories.b: Saudi Arabia and Pakistan formalized a Memorandum of Understanding aimed at deepening bilateral cooperation and intelligence sharing in the field of cybersecurity.
stories.w: Enhanced international alliances help GCC authorities secure critical infrastructure against increasingly sophisticated cross-border threat actors.

stories.t: Saudi Red Crescent and Oracle Sign Cloud and AI MoU
stories.b: The Saudi Red Crescent Authority signed a strategic partnership agreement with Oracle to integrate advanced cloud computing and artificial intelligence solutions into emergency operations.
stories.w: Demonstrates how government agencies are modernizing mission-critical dispatch and response systems via enterprise hyperscale cloud partnerships.

stories.t: e& Launches First Offline-Capable AI Laptop in UAE
stories.b: Telecommunications operator e& introduced the UAE market's first AI-powered laptop capable of performing complex machine learning workloads without requiring an active internet connection.
stories.w: Highlights the commercial shift toward edge AI devices, presenting new opportunities for enterprise mobility and secure local data processing.

stories.t: King Salman Park Foundation and Huawei Partner on Smart Park AI
stories.b: The King Salman Park Foundation partnered with Huawei Saudi Arabia to incorporate smart infrastructure and AI-driven management systems into Riyadh's urban green space development.
stories.w: Showcases the integration of IoT and AI in large-scale urban development projects aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 smart city mandates.

stories.t: TRA Issues Number Portability Regulatory Framework
stories.b: Oman’s Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) officially released a comprehensive regulatory framework governing mobile number portability to foster market competition.
stories.w: Establishes clearer compliance guidelines for telecom operators and safeguards consumer choice in Oman's evolving digital communications market.

stories.t: CBB and NCSC Organize Joint Cybersecurity Workshop
stories.b: The Central Bank of Bahrain (CBB), in collaboration with the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), hosted a specialized workshop to strengthen institutional cyber resilience across financial institutions.
stories.w: Reinforces regulatory expectations for banks to maintain rigorous defensive posture against rising digital threats.

stories.t: Anthropic Launches New Version of AI Model
stories.b: Anthropic announced the release of an upgraded iteration of its foundational AI model family, attracting regional technology agency coverage across Qatar.
stories.w: Provides enterprise architects in Gulf institutions with advanced model alternatives for specialized, secure LLM deployments.

themes.t: Industrial AI Scaling and Enterprise Adoption
themes.b: The Gulf region has shifted decisively from AI experimentation to heavy execution, highlighted by major infrastructure setups like NTT DATA's AI Factory Lab in Riyadh and mass workforce training initiatives such as Dubai Chambers' Agentic AI programme. Partnerships between government entities, cloud providers, and telecom operators underscore a regional push toward localized, high-impact machine learning deployment.

themes.t: Sovereign Financial Depth and Capital Markets
themes.b: Strong capital market activity, anchored by Saudi Arabia's $3.25 billion dual-tranche USD sukuk issuance, demonstrates robust international investor confidence in Gulf sovereign debt. This liquidity underpins extensive government spending on digital transformation, smart city initiatives, and national infrastructure projects.

Regulatory bodies and central banks across the GCC are intensifying cooperation with national security agencies to fortify critical sectors. Joint initiatives, such as Bahrain's CBB-NCSC workshop and Saudi-Pakistani cybersecurity MoUs, reflect an urgent priority to protect financial systems and government clouds against sophisticated threats.

items: Evaluate local hyperscale cloud and AI factory offerings, such as the upcoming NTT DATA lab in Riyadh, to optimize enterprise AI latency and compliance.
Assess edge-AI hardware integration strategies following the release of offline-capable AI client devices in the UAE market.
Review enterprise infrastructure scalability to ensure readiness for autonomous 'Agentic AI' enterprise workloads.
Align internal cybersecurity frameworks with recent central bank and national cyber center guidelines, incorporating insights from regional collaborative workshops.
Audit cross-border data transfer protocols and third-party vendor risk management in light of new international security partnerships.
Strengthen operational resilience measures against advanced threat vectors targeting financial messaging and cloud environments.
Develop governance frameworks tailored for autonomous agentic AI systems deployed across commercial and government workflows.
Establish rigorous data sovereignty and localization pipelines to comply with evolving regional cloud adoption standards.
Curate high-quality localized datasets to maximize the operational accuracy of newly introduced foundational LLMs.
Incorporate large-scale AI workforce upskilling initiatives—similar to Dubai Chambers' 14,000-company training model—into internal change management roadmaps.
Align digital transformation milestones with broader national economic visions, leveraging favorable regional liquidity and sukuk-backed funding environments.
Streamline operational workflows by integrating advanced cloud and AI solutions modelled after recent public sector partnerships.

market.b: Marked by aggressive infrastructure expansion, including Riyadh's new AI factory lab, enterprise agentic training programs, and local edge-AI device rollouts.
Bolstered by successful multi-billion dollar sovereign sukuk issuances that set favorable benchmark pricing and liquidity metrics across the GCC.
Characterized by heightened regulatory oversight, joint national security workshops, and formal bilateral cooperation agreements to protect critical infrastructure.
Accelerated adoption of hyperscale cloud and AI solutions by public sector bodies, exemplified by emergency services and urban smart park integrations.

ceo.lead: If I were advising the CEO of a Gulf bank or government technology organisation, the three issues I would put on the leadership agenda this week are...
items: Capitalizing on the deep liquidity in regional debt markets to secure cost-effective financing for ongoing digital and AI infrastructure investments.
Scaling internal workforce readiness for autonomous agentic AI workflows to ensure productivity gains outpace implementation costs.
Elevating board-level oversight on cross-border cybersecurity compliance in response to heightened regulatory coordination across GCC central banks.
